What We Do

Full-Service Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) and SNF Revenue Cycle Management

Nursing home billing covers two parallel tracks: the facility PDPM payment system and the physician professional fee billing for nursing facility visits. PMEX manages physician E/M coding across the care continuum and coordinates with the facility billing team on PDPM episode accuracy.

Nursing Facility E/M Coding

Initial (99304 to 99306) and subsequent (99307 to 99310) nursing facility visits coded correctly.

SNF Admission Coding

Initial nursing facility care coded at correct complexity from the admission evaluation.

Discharge Day Billing

Nursing facility discharge codes (99315 to 99316) applied per documented discharge time.

Annual Assessment Coding

Annual nursing facility assessments coded separately from routine monthly visits.

PDPM Coordination

Physician billing coordinated with facility PDPM team on ICD-10 accuracy for case-mix.

Telehealth SNF Visits

Modifier 95 applied for remote SNF physician visits where payer coverage is confirmed.

Sound Familiar?

Common Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Every nursing facility subsequent visit defaulted to level 1 (99307) regardless of complexity.

PMEX codes subsequent nursing facility visits from MDM complexity, applying level 2 to 4 when the documentation supports it.

Annual nursing facility assessments billed as standard monthly visits, losing the higher assessment rate.

PMEX identifies annual assessment visits from the clinical calendar and codes them separately at the correct assessment E/M level.

Physician visit ICD-10 codes not aligned with the facility MDS, creating case-mix discrepancies.

PMEX coordinates physician ICD-10 coding with the facility MDS team to ensure diagnosis consistency across the PDPM case-mix grouper.

Telehealth SNF visits submitted without confirming payer coverage for remote nursing facility visits.

PMEX verifies SNF telehealth coverage per payer before billing remote visits with modifier 95.

Hospice election not flagged, causing physician billing claims to be denied as duplicative.

PMEX tracks hospice election dates per patient and routes physician billing to the correct hospice or attending physician framework.

New physician seeing an established SNF patient billed as an established visit, losing the new patient rate.

PMEX applies new patient codes for the first encounter between a physician and an SNF patient not seen in the prior 3 years.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) Billing

Nursing home physician billing loses 16 to 26 percent of revenue to visit level defaults, assessment miscoding, and hospice billing conflicts.

PATTERN 01

Subsequent Visit Defaulted to Level 1 on Every SNF Patient

All subsequent nursing facility visits submitted as 99307 regardless of clinical complexity. Patients with multiple active problems, medication management decisions, and acute-on-chronic conditions qualify for 99308 to 99310. Revenue difference: $35 to $90 per visit.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX codes every subsequent nursing facility visit from the documented MDM: problems addressed, data reviewed, and risk of management. Level 2 to 4 is applied when the progress note supports higher complexity.

PATTERN 02

Hospice Patient Billed to Medicare Part B Incorrectly

Patient enrolled in hospice. Attending physician continues billing Medicare Part B for routine nursing facility visits. Medicare denies: services related to the terminal diagnosis are covered under the hospice benefit, not Part B. Revenue at risk for recoupment.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks hospice election dates per patient and confirms whether the physician is the hospice attending physician or an independent attending. Billing is routed to the correct benefit structure for each visit.

PATTERN 03

Annual Nursing Facility Assessment Not Separately Billed

Physician performs the required annual comprehensive assessment. Bills 99307 (routine subsequent visit). Annual assessment qualifies for a higher-level E/M code when the documentation reflects the comprehensive evaluation. $55 per assessment in revenue not captured.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies annual assessment visits from the visit documentation and clinical calendar, coding them at the E/M level that reflects the comprehensiveness of the documented evaluation.

Questions

Nursing Home Billing Questions Answered

Using 2021 MDM criteria. Level 1 (99307): straightforward. Level 2 (99308): low complexity. Level 3 (99309): moderate complexity. Level 4 (99310): high complexity. The level is coded from the documented problems, data review, and management risk.

PDPM (Patient-Driven Payment Model) is the SNF facility payment system. Physician billing is separate under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule. We coordinate ICD-10 coding with the facility team to ensure diagnosis consistency for PDPM case-mix grouping.

When a patient is enrolled in hospice, physician billing for services related to the terminal diagnosis is covered under the hospice benefit. We track hospice election per patient and route claims to the correct benefit structure.
